      Rogue:{hitDie:8,saves:['dex','int'],skills:['acrobatics','athletics','deception','insight','intimidation','investigation','perception','performance','persuasion','sleightOfHand','stealth'],skillCount:4,features:['Expertise','Sneak Attack',"Thieves' Cant"]},
      Sorcerer:{hitDie:6,saves:['con','cha'],skills:['arcana','deception','insight','intimidation','persuasion','religion'],skillCount:2,features:['Spellcasting','Sorcerous Origin']},
      Warlock:{hitDie:8,saves:['wis','cha'],skills:['arcana','deception','history','intimidation','investigation','nature','religion'],skillCount:2,features:['Otherworldly Patron','Pact Magic']},
      Wizard:{hitDie:6,saves:['int','wis'],skills:['arcana','history','insight','investigation','medicine','religion'],skillCount:2,features:['Spellcasting','Arcane Recovery']}
    };
    const CHARACTER_SPECIES = [
      {name:'Hill Dwarf',speed:25,bonuses:{con:2,wis:1},features:['Darkvision','Dwarven Resilience','Stonecunning','Dwarven Toughness']},
      {name:'Mountain Dwarf',speed:25,bonuses:{con:2,str:2},features:['Darkvision','Dwarven Resilience','Dwarven Combat Training','Stonecunning','Dwarven Armor Training']},
      {name:'High Elf',speed:30,bonuses:{dex:2,int:1},features:['Darkvision','Keen Senses','Fey Ancestry','Trance','Elf Weapon Training','Cantrip']},
      {name:'Wood Elf',speed:35,bonuses:{dex:2,wis:1},features:['Darkvision','Keen Senses','Fey Ancestry','Trance','Elf Weapon Training','Fleet of Foot','Mask of the Wild']},
          spellbook.forEach(spell=>spells.push(`Spellbook: ${spell}`));
          const preparedCount=Math.max(1,1+abilityModifier(abilities.int));
          shuffle(spellbook).slice(0,preparedCount).forEach(spell=>spells.push(`Prepared 1st-level spell: ${spell}`))
        }
      }
      if(species.name==='Tiefling')spells.push('Racial cantrip: Thaumaturgy');
      if(species.name==='High Elf')spells.push(`Racial cantrip: ${randomItem(CHARACTER_SPELLS.Wizard.cantrips)}`);
      if(species.name==='Forest Gnome')spells.push('Racial cantrip: Minor Illusion');
      if(className==='Cleric'){
        const domainSpells={Life:['Bless','Cure Wounds'],Light:['Burning Hands','Faerie Fire'],Trickery:['Charm Person','Disguise Self']}[subclass];
        domainSpells.forEach(spell=>spells.push(`Domain spell: ${spell}`))
      }
      const features=[...classData.features,...(species.features||[])];
      if(className==='Cleric')features.push(...({Life:['Heavy Armor Proficiency','Disciple of Life'],Light:['Bonus Cantrip: Light','Warding Flare'],Trickery:['Blessing of the Trickster']}[subclass]));
      if(className==='Sorcerer')features.push(...(draconicOrigin?['Draconic Resilience','Draconic Ancestor']:['Wild Magic Surge','Tides of Chaos']));
      if(className==='Warlock')features.push(...({Archfey:['Fey Presence'],Fiend:["Dark One's Blessing"],'Great Old One':['Awakened Mind']}[subclass]));
      const backgroundGear=BACKGROUND_STARTING_GEAR[background.name];
      return {
        ...clone(CHARACTER_DEFAULTS),id,ownerPlayerId,name:randomCharacterName(nameExclusions),class:className,level:1,
        species:species.name,background:background.name,subclass,alignment:randomItem(['Lawful Good','Neutral Good','Chaotic Good','Lawful Neutral','True Neutral','Chaotic Neutral','Lawful Evil','Neutral Evil','Chaotic Evil']),
        speed:species.speed,hitDice:`1d${classData.hitDie}`,proficiencyBonus:2,initiative:dexterityModifier,ac:armorClass,
        hp:hitPoints,maxHp:hitPoints,notes,location,inspiration:false,abilities,saves,skills,features,
        inventory:[...CLASS_STARTING_GEAR[className],...backgroundGear.items],currency:backgroundGear.currency,spells,
        spellSlots:magic?`${magic.slots} 1st-level slot${magic.slots===1?'':'s'}`:'',
        creationVersion:1
      }
    }
    const defaults = {
      version:4,
      campaign:{id:uid('campaign'),name:'The Black Lantern',started:false,preset:'heroic',joinCode:'',session:1,canonicalSeq:0,aiUsage:{responses:0,inputTokens:0,outputTokens:0,totalTokens:0,byModel:{}},settings:clone(PRESETS.heroic.settings),permissions:{playersEditOwnCharacter:true,playersChangePortrait:true,playersDrawShared:true,playersSuggestSettings:true,playersChangeCampaign:false,partyControlAbsent:false,dmControlAbsent:false}},
      localPlayer:{id:localPlayerId,name:'Player',characterId:defaultCharacterId},
      characters:[createRandomCharacter({id:defaultCharacterId,ownerPlayerId:localPlayerId})],
      scene:{title:'Lantern Room',text:'A warm room with an old oak table and too many stories waiting to happen.',location:'Lantern Room'},
      messages:[],
      nextMoves:[],rollRequest:null,cards:[],quests:[],inventory:[],journal:'',visualPrompts:[],assets:[],
      timeline:[{id:uid('evt'),at:nowISO(),session:1,type:'campaign',actor:'Table',actorId:null,location:'Lantern Room',summary:'The table was opened.'}],
      atmosphere:{theme:'lantern',effects:['lantern','dust'],intensity:.25,reason:'Warm starting table'},
      ui:{dmThemeControl:true,effectsEnabled:true,motion:true,effectIntensity:35,manualEffects:[],manualEffectsOverride:false,colorMode:'follow'},
      audio:{mode:'off',voice:'',style:'creepy',autoNarrate:false},
      multiplayer:{role:'solo',room:'',hostOnline:false,lastRoom:'',lastCanonicalSeq:0,peers:{}},
      prep:{nearbyLocations:'deferred',importantNPCs:'deferred',rumors:'deferred',firstEncounter:'deferred'}
    };
    
    function mergeDefaults(base, value){
      if(Array.isArray(base)) return Array.isArray(value)?value:clone(base);
      if(base && typeof base==='object'){const out={};for(const k of Object.keys(base))out[k]=mergeDefaults(base[k],value?.[k]);for(const k of Object.keys(value||{}))if(!(k in out))out[k]=value[k];return out}
      return value===undefined?base:value;
    }
    let state=mergeDefaults(defaults, readStoredCampaign());
    function normalizeCharacter(character={}){return mergeDefaults(CHARACTER_DEFAULTS,character)}
    const charactersBeforeMigration=state.characters;
    let migratedCharacterCreation=false;
    state.characters=charactersBeforeMigration.map((character,index)=>{
      const normalized=normalizeCharacter(character);
      if(normalized.creationVersion==null&&!normalized.species&&!normalized.background){
        const otherNames=charactersBeforeMigration.filter((_,otherIndex)=>otherIndex!==index).map(other=>other.name);
        const generated=createRandomCharacter({id:normalized.id,ownerPlayerId:normalized.ownerPlayerId,location:normalized.location||state.scene.location,nameExclusions:otherNames,notes:normalized.notes||''});
        const existingName=String(normalized.name||'').trim();
        generated.name=existingName&&!otherNames.some(name=>String(name||'').trim().toLocaleLowerCase()===existingName.toLocaleLowerCase())?existingName:randomCharacterName(otherNames);
        generated.portraitAssetId=normalized.portraitAssetId||null;
        migratedCharacterCreation=true;
        return generated
      }
      return normalized
    });
    if(migratedCharacterCreation)localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY,JSON.stringify(state));
    if(!state.campaign.joinCode) state.campaign.joinCode=makeRoomCode();
    state.ui.manualEffectsOverride=!!state.ui.manualEffectsOverride;
    state.messages=state.messages.filter(m=>!(m.who==='DM'&&/Welcome to the table/i.test(m.text||'')&&/Choose what kind of story/i.test(m.text||'')));
    let appConfig={mode:'standalone',companion_origin:'http://127.0.0.1:8765',signaling:false,multi_replica:false};
    let session={connected:false,models:[],model:null};
    let dmAborter=null;
    let timelineMode='events';
    let streamMessage=null;
    let streamNode=null;
    let transcriptNodes=new Map();
    let transcriptRenderQueued=false;
    let transcriptScrollIntent=0;
    let toolCards=[];
    
    function campaignIndex(){try{const value=JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(CAMPAIGN_INDEX_KEY)||'[]');return Array.isArray(value)?value:[]}catch{return []}}
    function persistCampaignSnapshot(snapshot=state){if(!snapshot?.campaign?.id||rtc.role==='player'&&rtc.awaitingSnapshotAck)return;const id=snapshot.campaign.id,now=Date.now(),players=(snapshot.characters||[]).filter(ch=>ch.ownerPlayerId&&ch.ownerPlayerId!==snapshot.localPlayer?.id).map(ch=>({id:ch.ownerPlayerId,name:ch.name||'Player'})),index=campaignIndex(),old=index.find(entry=>entry.id===id),entry={id,title:snapshot.campaign.name||'Untitled campaign',room:snapshot.campaign.joinCode||snapshot.multiplayer?.lastRoom||'',role:snapshot.multiplayer?.role||'solo',started:!!snapshot.campaign.started,players,updatedAt:now,createdAt:old?.createdAt||now};localStorage.setItem(CAMPAIGN_STATE_PREFIX+id,JSON.stringify(snapshot));localStorage.setItem(CAMPAIGN_ACTIVE_KEY,id);localStorage.setItem(CAMPAIGN_INDEX_KEY,JSON.stringify([entry,...index.filter(item=>item.id!==id)]));localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY,JSON.stringify({campaignArchiveVersion:1}))}
    function save({broadcast=true}={}){const publish=broadcast&&rtc.role==='host';if(publish)state.campaign.canonicalSeq=(Number(state.campaign.canonicalSeq)||0)+1;persistCampaignSnapshot();flashSave();if(publish)rtc.publishCanonicalEvent()}
    function flashSave(){$('saveDot').className='status-dot';$('saveText').textContent='Saved locally'}
    function toast(text){const el=document.createElement('div');el.className='toast physics-pop';el.textContent=text;$('toastStack').append(el);setTimeout(()=>el.remove(),3200)}
    function makeRoomCode(){const alphabet='ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789';let s='';for(let i=0;i<7;i++)s+=alphabet[Math.floor(Math.random()*alphabet.length)];return s.slice(0,4)+'-'+s.slice(4)}
    function currentCharacter(){return state.characters.find(c=>c.id===state.localPlayer.characterId)||state.characters[0]}
    function addEvent(type,summary,{actor=state.localPlayer.name,actorId=state.localPlayer.id,location=state.scene.location||state.scene.title}={}){state.timeline.push({id:uid('evt'),at:nowISO(),session:state.campaign.session,type,actor,actorId,location,summary});if(state.timeline.length>5000)state.timeline=state.timeline.slice(-5000)}
    function sanitizedState(){const out=clone(state);out.audio=undefined;out.ui=undefined;out.multiplayer={role:'replica',room:state.campaign.joinCode,hostOnline:true,peers:{}};return out}
    
    // Minimal Markdown renderer: escapes HTML first, then applies a safe subset.
    function markdown(src=''){
      let s=esc(src).replace(/```([\s\S]*?)```/g,'<pre><code>$1</code></pre>');
      s=s.replace(/^### (.*)$/gm,'<h3>$1</h3>').replace(/^## (.*)$/gm,'<h2>$1</h2>').replace(/^# (.*)$/gm,'<h1>$1</h1>');
      s=s.replace(/^&gt; (.*)$/gm,'<blockquote>$1</blockquote>');
      s=s.replace(/\*\*(.*?)\*\*/g,'<strong>$1</strong>').replace(/\*(.*?)\*/g,'<em>$1</em>').replace(/`([^`]+)`/g,'<code>$1</code>');
      const lines=s.split('\n');let out=[],inUl=false,inOl=false;
      for(const line of lines){
        if(/^[-*] /.test(line)){if(!inUl){out.push('<ul>');inUl=true}out.push(`<li>${line.slice(2)}</li>`);continue}else if(inUl){out.push('</ul>');inUl=false}
        if(/^\d+\. /.test(line)){if(!inOl){out.push('<ol>');inOl=true}out.push(`<li>${line.replace(/^\d+\. /,'')}</li>`);continue}else if(inOl){out.push('</ol>');inOl=false}
        if(/^<(h\d|blockquote|pre)/.test(line)||/^<\/(h\d|blockquote|pre)/.test(line)){out.push(line);continue}
        if(line.trim())out.push(`<p>${line}</p>`)
      }
      if(inUl)out.push('</ul>');if(inOl)out.push('</ol>');return out.join('');
    }
    
    function render(){
      const c=currentCharacter();
      $('campaignMini').textContent=state.campaign.name;
      $('topSceneTitle').textContent=state.scene.title;$('sceneTitle').textContent=state.scene.title;$('sceneText').textContent=state.scene.text;
      $('sceneBadges').innerHTML=`<span class="chip">${esc(state.scene.location||state.scene.title)}</span><span class="chip">Session ${state.campaign.session}</span><span class="chip">${esc(state.campaign.settings.difficulty)}</span>`;
    <!doctype html>
    <html lang="en" class="booting">
    <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width,initial-scale=1,viewport-fit=cover" />
    <meta name="theme-color" content="#0d1017" />
    <title>Lantern Table — local-first D&D</title>
    <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/assets/logo.svg?v=1" />
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/app.css?v=narration-activity-spinner-1" />

    <body>
    <canvas id="shaderCanvas" class="ambient-canvas shader-canvas" aria-hidden="true"></canvas>
    <canvas id="fxCanvas" class="ambient-canvas fx-canvas" aria-hidden="true"></canvas>

        <div class="eyebrow">Joining table</div>
        <h1 id="joinOverlayTitle">Finding the host…</h1>
        <p id="joinOverlayText">Connecting to the table without creating a new campaign.</p>

    </div>

          <div><div class="eyebrow">Start fast · change anything later</div><h1 id="wizardTitle">What kind of table are we opening?</h1></div>
        </div>
        <p class="lede">Pick a starting shape. Lantern Table only asks for what the first scene needs; the DM fills in details lazily as you play.</p>
        <div id="presetGrid" class="preset-grid"></div>
        <details class="wizard-customize">
          <summary>Customize before starting</summary>
          <div class="form-grid two">
            <label>Campaign name<input id="wizName" value="The Black Lantern" /></label>
            <label>Difficulty<select id="wizDifficulty"><option>Relaxed</option><option selected>Normal</option><option>Dangerous</option><option>Brutal</option></select></label>
            <label>Rules style<select id="wizRules"><option>Story first</option><option selected>Balanced</option><option>Rules strict</option></select></label>
            <label>DM style<select id="wizDm"><option>Helpful</option><option selected>Neutral</option><option>Mischievous</option><option>Ruthless</option></select></label>
            <label>Description<select id="wizDesc"><option>Concise</option><option selected>Balanced</option><option>Cinematic</option></select></label>
            <label>Character creation<select id="wizChar"><option selected>Quick</option><option>Guided</option><option>Full</option></select></label>
          </div>
        </details>
        <div class="wizard-actions"><button id="wizardStart" class="button primary large">Open the table</button><span class="muted">You can edit these in Campaign Settings later.</span></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    
    <div class="app-shell" id="appShell">

        </button>

            </div>

        </section>
    
        <section id="view-campaign" class="view content-view">
          <div class="view-heading"><div><div class="eyebrow">Host controls</div><h1>Campaign</h1><p>Set direction, permissions, and table rules. Nothing here is permanent.</p></div><button id="reopenWizard" class="button">Quick presets</button></div>

    async def choose_model(creds: dict[str, Any], requested: str | None) -> str:
        if requested:
            return requested
        models = await list_models(creds)
        if not models:
            raise HTTPException(400, "No eligible models were returned for this ChatGPT account")
        return models[0]["slug"]
    
    
    def sse(event: str, data: Any) -> str:
        payload = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
        return f"event: {event}\ndata: {payload}\n\n"

    async def _room_publish(room: str, message: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        if redis_client:
            await redis_client.publish(f"lantern:room:{room}", json.dumps(message, separators=(",", ":")))
        if opening:
            history.append({"role": "user", "content": f"[TABLE DIRECTIVE — do not quote this instruction] {opening}"})
        for message in body.get("messages", [])[-20:]:
            if message.get("who") == "System":
                continue
            role = "assistant" if message.get("kind") == "dm" else "user"
            text = str(message.get("text", "")).strip()
            if text:
                history.append({"role": role, "content": text})
        return history
    
    
    def dm_instructions(body: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        settings = body.get("campaign_settings", {})
        return f"""You are the Dungeon Master for a collaborative tabletop fantasy RPG named {body.get('campaign', 'Lantern Table')}.
    
    PLAY STYLE
    - Write the spoken/narrated part of every turn as clean Markdown. Use short headings, emphasis, blockquotes, lists, and tables only when they improve playability.
    - Be vivid but interactive: usually 2-6 short paragraphs. Never decide a player character's thoughts, dialogue, or choices.
    - Treat each player message as an attempted action, not as authority over the world. The player controls their character's intent; you adjudicate whether it is possible, what it costs, what roll or resource is required, and what happens. Do not grant success merely because the player states an outcome.
    - Players cannot declare changes to weather, time, location, NPC behavior, monsters, treasure, or other characters. Such changes require an established fictional cause and a capability the character actually has (for example, a listed spell or feature with the required resources). If the capability is absent or the effect exceeds it, explain the limit in the fiction and offer valid alternatives.
    - Keep atmospheric presentation separate from game facts. Never use set_atmosphere to make weather happen; use it only to reflect weather or mood already established in the scene. Do not let a player's request itself establish a storm, sunshine, or other environmental change.
    - Respect the campaign controls: {json.dumps(settings, ensure_ascii=False)}
    - The campaign is intentionally lazy-built. Invent only what is needed now, preserve established facts, and let the table add detail later.
    - Do not fabricate dice results. Use request_roll only when uncertainty matters.
    - Use the 2014 D&D 5e Basic Rules as the default rules baseline for this campaign. Apply the actual character sheet, listed spells/features, action economy, movement, range, components, duration, concentration, conditions, rests, and expendable resources before resolving an attempt. Do not invent a spell, feature, proficiency, bonus, or resource. If a rule or character detail is missing, ask a brief question or make a conservative ruling and state it.
    - For a skill check, name the actual skill in request_roll so the app can add proficiency from the sheet; use skill NONE for a raw ability check. Set saving_throw true only for a saving throw, allowing the app to apply saving throw proficiency.
    - Call for a check only when an allowed attempt has a meaningful uncertain outcome. State the relevant ability/skill and stakes; do not call for a roll when an action is impossible, automatic, or has no meaningful consequence. Resolve the roll against a clear DC, and do not treat a natural 1 or 20 as automatic failure or success on an ability check.
    - In combat, track turns and action economy; a character gets movement and one action on their turn, and a bonus action exists only when a rule grants one. Resolve attacks against AC and apply listed damage/effects. Do not let a player take another turn or spend a resource they do not have.
    - Players own character identity/background, but mechanical fields (HP, max HP, AC, level, conditions, location) are game-authoritative. Use set_character_mechanics to establish/correct starting stats and propose_state_patch for damage/healing.
    - Treat local host state as authoritative.
    
    UI AND GAME TOOLS
    - Always call set_next_moves exactly once per DM turn with exactly 3 distinct, specific options. Make them useful responses to the current situation (for example, a cautious approach, a direct approach, and a creative/social approach when those fit). Describe consequences or tradeoffs briefly. The options are suggestions, not a menu that limits free-form player intent. End narration by asking what the players do.
    - Use render_card for important NPCs, monsters, clues, items, factions, quests, or locations when a compact reference helps.
    - Use propose_state_patch for durable changes. When applying HP changes, name the affected character. Keep patches small and explain why.
    - Use set_character_mechanics when a new quick-start character needs authoritative starting HP/AC/level. Do this early in the opening if the sheet still has placeholder mechanics.
    - Use suggest_visual_prompt when art would materially help. Lantern Table does not generate images; provide a polished prompt for the user to copy elsewhere.
    
    ATMOSPHERE TOOL
    Use set_atmosphere only on meaningful environmental/emotional transitions, not every turn. It changes presentation only; it never changes campaign facts or grants a character control over the environment. Player devices may opt out. Choose for readability first, mood second. A theme is a scene-lighting cue, not a reward animation. Preserve a theme across nearby rooms unless mood or environment materially changes.
    
    Theme families and suggested story use:
    
    - wet: soaked/rain-slick surfaces or a scene emerging from water; use for actual wetness, not merely water nearby.
    - fire: active flames consuming or touching the scene; embers remain the quieter nearby-fire cue.
    - cold: ice, frost, freezing magic, or extreme cold; distinct from falling snow.
    - hot: unbearable heat, lava proximity, or red-hot metal such as Heat Metal; prefer this over fire when the object is glowing hot rather than burning.
    - acid: active corrosive liquid, acid spray/pools, or dissolving surfaces.
    - poison: toxic gas, venomous haze, or poisoned environs; Cloudkill-like scenes may pair poison + fog.
    - radiant: searing holy/celestial power or radiant energy; bright but never allowed to wash out readable UI.
    - necrotic: life-draining, undead, deathly, or withering magic.
    - lightning: magical/electrical charge and lightning damage; storm remains actual weather.
    - thunder: brief concussive sonic shockwaves; use sparingly for impact beats, not as a persistent wallpaper.
    - force: pure magical force, barriers, telekinetic pressure, or force damage.
    - psychic: mind-rending, dream logic, telepathy overload, or psychic damage; keep intensity restrained for readability.
    - darkness: magical darkness or strongly obscured supernatural shadow; presentation must preserve legible cards and controls.
    - web: thick sticky webbing, restrained/webbed spaces, or web-covered surfaces. Webs can coexist with fire briefly when fiction says they ignite.
    - grease: magically/oily slippery surfaces and Grease-like difficult terrain.
    - faerie: Faerie Fire-like blue/green/violet outlining, glittering revelation, or anti-invisibility reveal.
    - petrified: stone transformation, petrification, statues awakening, or stone curse environments.
    - Hearth / refuge / human warmth: lantern, black-gold, white-gold, gruvbox-dark/light, autumn. Pair lantern + dust; embers only when fire is present.
    - Crypt / horror / oppressive darkness: dracula, ash, matte-black, pitch-black, rose-pine-moon, halloween. Pair fog/dust/lantern; use storm only for actual weather or a supernatural shock.
    - Winter / ice / exposed mountains: winter-frost, nord-dark/light, graphite-dark/light. Pair snow/fog; keep intensity low during dialogue.
    - Forest / earth / old natural magic: everforest-dark/light, kanagawa-wave/dragon/lotus, mist-gb. Pair fireflies/dust/fog.
    - Rain / city / ship / nocturnal travel: tokyo-night-storm, tokyo-night, night-owl, nord-dark. Pair rain and occasional storm.
    - Ocean / flooded ruins / reflective shores: rose-pine-moon, berry-nebula, kanagawa-wave, summer-beach. Use water for shore/reflection; underwater + bubbles only when actually submerged.
    - Arcane / dream / cosmic / planar: berry-nebula, catppuccin-mocha/macchiato/frappe, rose-pine, inkpink, sweet, twilight-5. Pair stars/aurora/fireflies.
    - Bright daylight / social / hopeful: ayu-light, rose-pine-dawn, github-light, catppuccin-latte, serika-light, modus-operandi, whitesur-light, graphite-light, white-gold, summer-beach. Prefer no effects or very subtle dust.
    - Combat / fire / destruction / urgency: autumn, black-gold, gruvbox-dark, ayu-dark, midnight-ablaze, lava-gb, rust-gold-8. Pair embers/dust; never use constant flashing.
    - Machinery / strange technology / glitch: tokyo-night, one-dark, graphite-dark, matte-black, 2bit-demichrome, pico-8, nintendo-gameboy, slso8. Usually use no weather; stars/aurora only for explicitly digital/cosmic scenes.
    - Ceremony / festival / celebration: diwali, lunar-new-year, christmas, hanukkah, st-patricks-day, valentine, blessing. Use effects that match the fiction rather than the palette name.
    - Retro / surreal / stylized one-off scenes: oil-6, pollen8, vinik24, mist-gb, lava-gb, 2bit-demichrome, pico-8, slso8. Use sparingly so they feel intentional.
    - Rhiannon-night is literary/celestial: near-black with warm cream, blush/lavender/gold feeling; use for magical, intimate, reflective scenes and soft starlight.
    
    Effect semantics:
    - snow: falling outdoor/ruined snow; rain: visible rainfall; dust: motes/age/sunbeams; embers: nearby heat/fire; fireflies: living magic/forest dusk; fog: obscured depth; lantern: warm local light; bubbles: submerged water; water: reflective/rippled surface; underwater: full-screen caustic/submerged feel; aurora: magical sky/planar glow; storm: rain plus brief lightning; stars: celestial/void ambience.
    - Do not stack more than 2-3 effects unless it is a brief climax. Never use storm merely to make combat exciting.
    - Transitions should usually be 900-2400ms. Use intensity 0.15-0.45 normally; exceed 0.65 only for short dramatic moments. If players need to read dense cards, lower effects instead of increasing them.
    
    CURRENT LOCAL STATE
    Scene: {json.dumps(body.get('scene', {}), ensure_ascii=False)}
    Characters: {json.dumps(body.get('characters', body.get('party', [])), ensure_ascii=False)}
    Quests: {json.dumps(body.get('quests', []), ensure_ascii=False)}
    Inventory: {json.dumps(body.get('inventory', []), ensure_ascii=False)}
    Recent timeline: {json.dumps(body.get('timeline', [])[-20:], ensure_ascii=False)}
    Recent journal: {str(body.get('journal', ''))[-5000:]}
    """
    
    
    @app.post("/api/dm/stream")
    async def api_dm_stream(request: Request):
        if MODE == "public":
            raise HTTPException(503, "Run the Lantern Table companion on the host device for ChatGPT-plan inference")
        creds = await auth_creds()
        body = await request.json()
        model = await choose_model(creds, body.get("model"))
        payload = {
            "model": model,
            "instructions": dm_instructions(body),
            "input": build_history(body),

    function makeRoomCode(){const alphabet='ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789';let s='';for(let i=0;i<7;i++)s+=alphabet[Math.floor(Math.random()*alphabet.length)];return s.slice(0,4)+'-'+s.slice(4)}
    function currentCharacter(){return state.characters.find(c=>c.id===state.localPlayer.characterId)||state.characters[0]}

    // Minimal Markdown renderer: escapes HTML first, then applies a safe subset.
    function markdown(src=''){
      let s=esc(src).replace(/```([\s\S]*?)```/g,'<pre><code>$1</code></pre>');
      s=s.replace(/^### (.*)$/gm,'<h3>$1</h3>').replace(/^## (.*)$/gm,'<h2>$1</h2>').replace(/^# (.*)$/gm,'<h1>$1</h1>');
      s=s.replace(/^&gt; (.*)$/gm,'<blockquote>$1</blockquote>');
      s=s.replace(/\*\*(.*?)\*\*/g,'<strong>$1</strong>').replace(/\*(.*?)\*/g,'<em>$1</em>').replace(/`([^`]+)`/g,'<code>$1</code>');
      const lines=s.split('\n');let out=[],inUl=false,inOl=false;
      for(const line of lines){
        if(/^[-*] /.test(line)){if(!inUl){out.push('<ul>');inUl=true}out.push(`<li>${line.slice(2)}</li>`);continue}else if(inUl){out.push('</ul>');inUl=false}
        if(/^\d+\. /.test(line)){if(!inOl){out.push('<ol>');inOl=true}out.push(`<li>${line.replace(/^\d+\. /,'')}</li>`);continue}else if(inOl){out.push('</ol>');inOl=false}
        if(/^<(h\d|blockquote|pre)/.test(line)||/^<\/(h\d|blockquote|pre)/.test(line)){out.push(line);continue}
        if(line.trim())out.push(`<p>${line}</p>`)
      }
      if(inUl)out.push('</ul>');if(inOl)out.push('</ol>');return out.join('');
    }

      renderTranscript();renderNextMoves();renderQuests();renderPresence();renderCharacter();renderCampaign();renderUsage();renderTimeline();renderGallery();renderSettings();renderAtmosphere();renderAI();renderMultiplayer();

      const online=!!session.connected,checking=!!session.checking,needsLogin=!!session.reachable&&!online;dot.className=`status-dot ${online?'':checking||needsLogin?'warn':'bad'}`;label.textContent=online?'DM connected':checking?'DM reconnecting…':needsLogin?'DM sign-in needed':'DM disconnected';
      if(!checking)dmConnectionLog(online?'connected':needsLogin?'sign-in needed':'offline');

    async def _room_publish(room: str, message: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        if redis_client:
            await redis_client.publish(f"lantern:room:{room}", json.dumps(message, separators=(",", ":")))
            return
        peers = local_room_peers.get(room, {})
        target = message.get("target")
        for route_id, ws in list(peers.items()):
            is_host = route_id.startswith("host:")
    
    PLAY STYLE
    - Write the spoken/narrated part of every turn as clean Markdown. Use short headings, emphasis, blockquotes, lists, and tables only when they improve playability.
    - Be vivid but interactive: usually 2-6 short paragraphs. Never decide a player character's thoughts, dialogue, or choices.
    - Treat each player message as an attempted action, not as authority over the world. The player controls their character's intent; you adjudicate whether it is possible, what it costs, what roll or resource is required, and what happens. Do not grant success merely because the player states an outcome.
    - Players cannot declare changes to weather, time, location, NPC behavior, monsters, treasure, or other characters. Such changes require an established fictional cause and a capability the character actually has (for example, a listed spell or feature with the required resources). If the capability is absent or the effect exceeds it, explain the limit in the fiction and offer valid alternatives.
    - Keep atmospheric presentation separate from game facts. Never use set_atmosphere to make weather happen; use it only to reflect weather or mood already established in the scene. Do not let a player's request itself establish a storm, sunshine, or other environmental change.
    - Respect the campaign controls: {json.dumps(settings, ensure_ascii=False)}
    - The campaign is intentionally lazy-built. Invent only what is needed now, preserve established facts, and let the table add detail later.
    - Do not fabricate dice results. Use request_roll only when uncertainty matters.
    - Use the 2014 D&D 5e Basic Rules as the default rules baseline for this campaign. Apply the actual character sheet, listed spells/features, action economy, movement, range, components, duration, concentration, conditions, rests, and expendable resources before resolving an attempt. Do not invent a spell, feature, proficiency, bonus, or resource. If a rule or character detail is missing, ask a brief question or make a conservative ruling and state it.
    - For a skill check, name the actual skill in request_roll so the app can add proficiency from the sheet; use skill NONE for a raw ability check. Set saving_throw true only for a saving throw, allowing the app to apply saving throw proficiency.
    - Call for a check only when an allowed attempt has a meaningful uncertain outcome. State the relevant ability/skill and stakes; do not call for a roll when an action is impossible, automatic, or has no meaningful consequence. Resolve the roll against a clear DC, and do not treat a natural 1 or 20 as automatic failure or success on an ability check.
    - In combat, track turns and action economy; a character gets movement and one action on their turn, and a bonus action exists only when a rule grants one. Resolve attacks against AC and apply listed damage/effects. Do not let a player take another turn or spend a resource they do not have.
    - Players own character identity/background, but mechanical fields (HP, max HP, AC, level, conditions, location) are game-authoritative. Use set_character_mechanics to establish/correct starting stats and propose_state_patch for damage/healing.
    - Treat local host state as authoritative.
    
    UI AND GAME TOOLS
    - Always call set_next_moves exactly once per DM turn with exactly 3 distinct, specific options. Make them useful responses to the current situation (for example, a cautious approach, a direct approach, and a creative/social approach when those fit). Describe consequences or tradeoffs briefly. The options are suggestions, not a menu that limits free-form player intent. End narration by asking what the players do.
    - Use render_card for important NPCs, monsters, clues, items, factions, quests, or locations when a compact reference helps.
    - Use propose_state_patch for durable changes. When applying HP changes, name the affected character. Keep patches small and explain why.
    - Use set_character_mechanics when a new quick-start character needs authoritative starting HP/AC/level. Do this early in the opening if the sheet still has placeholder mechanics.
    - Use suggest_visual_prompt when art would materially help. Lantern Table does not generate images; provide a polished prompt for the user to copy elsewhere.
    
    ATMOSPHERE TOOL
    Use set_atmosphere only on meaningful environmental/emotional transitions, not every turn. It changes presentation only; it never changes campaign facts or grants a character control over the environment. Player devices may opt out. Choose for readability first, mood second. A theme is a scene-lighting cue, not a reward animation. Preserve a theme across nearby rooms unless mood or environment materially changes.

      sendCanonicalWssSnapshot(peerId){

      async makeOffer(peerId,hello={}){

## Assistant

I found the main authority gap: the browser currently records player text and forwards it to the DM, while roll cards calculate a handful of modifiers locally and AI patches can directly change HP. I’m adding a pure rules module with injectable dice, auditable events, combat lifecycle, checks, saves, attacks, reactions, timeout, and death saves. In the app, combat intents will be host validated and broadcast through the existing canonical snapshot path; AI HP patches will be removed. I’ll also add a player-visible entity registry/directory while preserving existing PC sheet data.

    // Lantern Table's deterministic core for 2014 D&D 5e (SRD 5.1).
    // Rule text is not reproduced here; source metadata links to the official Basic Rules.
    export const RULE_SOURCES = Object.freeze({
      'srd5.1:how-to-play':'https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/introduction',
      'srd5.1:ability-check':'https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/using-ability-scores',
      'srd5.1:saving-throw':'https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/using-ability-scores',
      'srd5.1:combat:initiative':'https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/combat',
      'srd5.1:combat:turn':'https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/combat',
      'srd5.1:combat:attack':'https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/combat',
      'srd5.1:combat:dodge':'https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/combat',
      'srd5.1:combat:ready':'https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/combat',
      'srd5.1:combat:reaction':'https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/combat',
      'srd5.1:combat:death-save':'https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/combat',
      'srd5.1:condition:incapacitated':'https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/appendix-a-conditions',
      'srd5.1:condition:unconscious':'https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/appendix-a-conditions',
      'lantern:procedure:turn-timeout':null,
      'lantern:procedure:reaction-timeout':null
    });
    
    export const ACTIONS = Object.freeze(['Attack','Cast a Spell','Dash','Disengage','Dodge','Help','Hide','Ready','Search','Use an Object']);
    export const TURN_TIMEOUT_MS = 90_000;
    const ABILITIES = ['str','dex','con','int','wis','cha'];
    const uid = () => `mech_${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
    const die = sides => { const bytes = new Uint32Array(1); crypto.getRandomValues(bytes); return bytes[0] % sides + 1; };
    const roll = (sides, roller=die) => roller(sides);
    export const abilityModifier = score => Math.floor((Number(score || 10)-10)/2);
    const abilityScore = (c,a) => Number(c.abilityScores?.[a.toLowerCase()] ?? c.abilities?.[a.toLowerCase()] ?? 10);
    const proficient = (c,key) => (c.proficiencies||[]).includes(key) || !!c.skills?.[key] || !!c.saves?.[key];
    const event = (state,type,actorId,rule,intent,extra={}) => ({eventId:uid(),eventType:type,at:new Date().toISOString(),sourceRule:rule,combatId:state.combat?.combatId||null,turnId:state.combat?.turnId||null,actorId,targetIds:[],intent,mutations:[],...extra});
    const fail = reason => ({ok:false,reason,events:[]});
    const current = state => state.combat?.order?.[state.combat.activeIndex];
    const conditions = c => new Set((c.conditions||[]).map(x=>typeof x==='string'?x:x.name));
    export const hasCondition = (c,n) => conditions(c).has(n);
    export const incapacitated = c => ['incapacitated','unconscious','stunned','paralyzed'].some(n=>hasCondition(c,n));
    export function rollD20({modifier=0,advantage=false,disadvantage=false,roller=die}={}) {
      const dice = advantage===disadvantage ? [roll(20,roller)] : [roll(20,roller),roll(20,roller)];
      const kept = dice.length===1?dice[0]:(advantage?Math.max(...dice):Math.min(...dice));
      return {dice,raw:dice,kept,modifiers:[modifier],total:kept+modifier};

    import test from 'node:test';
    import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
    import * as rules from '../assets/rules5e.js';
    
    const actor=(id,extra={})=>({id,entityId:id,name:id,ownerPlayerId:id==='a'?'p':null,mechanicsReady:true,hp:10,maxHp:10,ac:12,speed:30,abilities:{str:14,dex:16,con:10},skills:{stealth:true},proficiencyBonus:2,...extra});
    const fixture=()=>({characters:[actor('a'),actor('b',{ownerPlayerId:null})],game:{phase:'freeplay'},timeline:[]});
    const fixed=(...values)=>sides=>{const value=values.shift()??10;assert.ok(value>=1&&value<=sides);return value};
    
    test('freeplay has no initiative lock and combat start uses stable initiative order',()=>{
      const state=fixture();assert.equal(state.game.phase,'freeplay');
      const result=rules.beginCombat(state,{roller:fixed(12,8)});assert.equal(result.ok,true);assert.equal(state.game.phase,'combat');
      const order=state.combat.order.map(x=>x.entityId);rules.startNextRoundTurn(state,{now:state.combat.turnStartedAt+1});assert.equal(state.combat.round,2);assert.deepEqual(state.combat.order.map(x=>x.entityId),order);
    });
    test('turn actions require active actor and current turn id; reactions can be used only once',()=>{
      const s=fixture();rules.beginCombat(s,{roller:fixed(12,8)});const active=s.combat.order[0],other=s.combat.order[1];
      assert.equal(rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:other.entityId,intent:{kind:'action',action:'Dodge'},turnId:s.combat.turnId}).ok,false);
      assert.match(rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:active.entityId,intent:{kind:'action',action:'Dodge'},turnId:'old'}).reason,/Stale/);
      assert.equal(rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:other.entityId,intent:{kind:'reaction',trigger:'opportunity_attack'},turnId:s.combat.turnId}).ok,true);
      assert.equal(rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:other.entityId,intent:{kind:'reaction',trigger:'opportunity_attack'},turnId:s.combat.turnId}).ok,false);
    });
    test('surprise is individual and ends after that creature first turn',()=>{
      const s=fixture();rules.beginCombat(s,{surprise:{b:true},roller:fixed(12,8)});const b=s.combat.order.find(x=>x.entityId==='b');
      s.combat.activeIndex=s.combat.order.indexOf(b);s.combat.turnId='bturn';
      assert.equal(rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:'b',turnId:'bturn',intent:{kind:'move',feet:1}}).ok,false);
      const first=rules.endTurn(s);assert.equal(first.ok,true);assert.equal(b.firstTurn,false);assert.equal('surpriseRound' in s.combat,false);
    });
    test('movement splits against budget, action is single, Delay is rejected, Ready spends action',()=>{
      const s=fixture();rules.beginCombat(s,{roller:fixed(12,8)});const a=s.combat.order[0].entityId;
      assert.equal(rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:a,turnId:s.combat.turnId,intent:{kind:'move',feet:10}}).ok,true);
      assert.equal(rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:a,turnId:s.combat.turnId,intent:{kind:'action',action:'Dodge'}}).ok,true);
      assert.equal(rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:a,turnId:s.combat.turnId,intent:{kind:'action',action:'Dash'}}).ok,false);
      const t=fixture();rules.beginCombat(t,{roller:fixed(12,8)});const id=t.combat.order[0].entityId;
      assert.match(rules.validateIntent(t,{actorId:id,turnId:t.combat.turnId,intent:{kind:'action',action:'Delay'}}).reason,/no Delay/);
      assert.equal(rules.validateIntent(t,{actorId:id,turnId:t.combat.turnId,intent:{kind:'action',action:'Ready',trigger:'when the door opens',response:'Attack'}}).ok,true);
    });
    test('checks derive modifiers and advantage rolls are auditable',()=>{
      const s=fixture();const r=rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:'a',roller:fixed(4,17),intent:{kind:'ability_check',ability:'dex',skill:'stealth',dc:15,advantage:true}});
      assert.equal(r.roll.total,22);assert.deepEqual(r.roll.dice,[4,17]);assert.deepEqual(r.roll.modifiers,[5]);assert.equal(r.result.success,true);
    });
    test('attacks honor range, natural 1 and 20, AC and apply damage only on hit',()=>{
      const s=fixture();rules.beginCombat(s,{roller:fixed(12,8)});const a=s.combat.order[0].entityId;s.combat.turnLocal.actionAvailable=true;
      assert.equal(rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:a,turnId:s.combat.turnId,roller:fixed(10),intent:{kind:'action',action:'Attack',targetId:'b',distance:40,range:5,damage:4}}).ok,false);
      let result=rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:a,turnId:s.combat.turnId,roller:fixed(1),intent:{kind:'action',action:'Attack',targetId:'b',distance:5,range:5,damage:4}});assert.equal(result.result.hit,false);assert.equal(s.characters[1].hp,10);
      s.combat.turnLocal.actionAvailable=true;result=rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:a,turnId:s.combat.turnId,roller:fixed(20),intent:{kind:'action',action:'Attack',targetId:'b',distance:5,range:5,damage:4}});assert.equal(result.result.critical,true);assert.equal(s.characters[1].hp,6);
    });
    test('surprise blocks action, incapacitation blocks action, timeout Dodges legally',()=>{
      const s=fixture();rules.beginCombat(s,{roller:fixed(12,8)});s.combat.turnDeadlineAt=0;const out=rules.handleTurnTimeout(s,{now:100,roller:fixed(10)});assert.equal(out.ok,true);assert.ok(out.events.some(x=>x.eventType==='turn_timed_out'&&x.sourceRule==='lantern:procedure:turn-timeout'));assert.ok(out.events.some(x=>x.eventType==='action_dodge'));
      const t=fixture();t.characters[0].conditions=['incapacitated'];rules.beginCombat(t,{roller:fixed(12,8)});t.combat.turnDeadlineAt=0;const event=rules.handleTurnTimeout(t,{now:100});assert.equal(event.events.some(x=>x.eventType==='action_dodge'),false);
    });
    test('death saves are mandatory and stable characters stop rolling',()=>{
      const s=fixture();s.characters[0].hp=0;s.characters[0].deathSaves={successes:0,failures:0,stable:false};
      const first=rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:'a',intent:{kind:'saving_throw',ability:'con',sourceRule:'srd5.1:combat:death-save'},roller:fixed(10)});assert.equal(first.ok,true);
      assert.equal(rules.abilityModifier(16),3);assert.equal(rules.abilityModifier(9),-1);
    });
    test('Dodge, Dash and Disengage use turn-local state and table reactions default to decline',()=>{
      const s=fixture();rules.beginCombat(s,{roller:fixed(12,8)});const a=s.combat.order[0].entityId;
      assert.equal(rules.validateIntent(s,{actorId:a,turnId:s.combat.turnId,intent:{kind:'action',action:'Dash'}}).ok,true);assert.equal(s.combat.turnLocal.movementRemaining,60);
      const declined=rules.dismissOptionalReaction(s,'a');assert.equal(declined.events[0].eventType,'reaction_declined');assert.equal(declined.events[0].sourceRule,'lantern:procedure:reaction-timeout');
    });

    PLAY STYLE
    - Write the spoken/narrated part of every turn as clean Markdown. Use short headings, emphasis, blockquotes, lists, and tables only when they improve playability.
    - Be vivid but interactive: usually 2-6 short paragraphs. Never decide a player character's thoughts, dialogue, or choices.
    - Treat each player message as an attempted action, not as authority over the world. The player controls their character's intent; you adjudicate whether it is possible, what it costs, what roll or resource is required, and what happens. Do not grant success merely because the player states an outcome.
    - Players cannot declare changes to weather, time, location, NPC behavior, monsters, treasure, or other characters. Such changes require an established fictional cause and a capability the character actually has (for example, a listed spell or feature with the required resources). If the capability is absent or the effect exceeds it, explain the limit in the fiction and offer valid alternatives.
    - Keep atmospheric presentation separate from game facts. Never use set_atmosphere to make weather happen; use it only to reflect weather or mood already established in the scene. Do not let a player's request itself establish a storm, sunshine, or other environmental change.
    - Respect the campaign controls: {json.dumps(settings, ensure_ascii=False)}
    - The campaign is intentionally lazy-built. Invent only what is needed now, preserve established facts, and let the table add detail later.
    - Do not fabricate dice results. Use request_roll only when uncertainty matters.
    - Use the 2014 D&D 5e Basic Rules as the default rules baseline for this campaign. Apply the actual character sheet, listed spells/features, action economy, movement, range, components, duration, concentration, conditions, rests, and expendable resources before resolving an attempt. Do not invent a spell, feature, proficiency, bonus, or resource. If a rule or character detail is missing, ask a brief question or make a conservative ruling and state it.
    - For a skill check, name the actual skill in request_roll so the app can add proficiency from the sheet; use skill NONE for a raw ability check. Set saving_throw true only for a saving throw, allowing the app to apply saving throw proficiency.
    - Call for a check only when an allowed attempt has a meaningful uncertain outcome. State the relevant ability/skill and stakes; do not call for a roll when an action is impossible, automatic, or has no meaningful consequence. Resolve the roll against a clear DC, and do not treat a natural 1 or 20 as automatic failure or success on an ability check.
    - In combat, track turns and action economy; a character gets movement and one action on their turn, and a bonus action exists only when a rule grants one. Resolve attacks against AC and apply listed damage/effects. Do not let a player take another turn or spend a resource they do not have.
    - Players own character identity/background, but mechanical fields (HP, max HP, AC, level, conditions, location) are game-authoritative. Use set_character_mechanics to establish/correct starting stats and propose_state_patch for damage/healing.
    - Treat local host state as authoritative.
    
    UI AND GAME TOOLS
    - Always call set_next_moves exactly once per DM turn with exactly 3 distinct, specific options. Make them useful responses to the current situation (for example, a cautious approach, a direct approach, and a creative/social approach when those fit). Describe consequences or tradeoffs briefly. The options are suggestions, not a menu that limits free-form player intent. End narration by asking what the players do.
    - Use render_card for important NPCs, monsters, clues, items, factions, quests, or locations when a compact reference helps.
    - Use propose_state_patch for durable changes. When applying HP changes, name the affected character. Keep patches small and explain why.
    - Use set_character_mechanics when a new quick-start character needs authoritative starting HP/AC/level. Do this early in the opening if the sheet still has placeholder mechanics.
    - Use suggest_visual_prompt when art would materially help. Lantern Table does not generate images; provide a polished prompt for the user to copy elsewhere.

     - The campaign is intentionally lazy-built. Invent only what is needed now, preserve established facts, and let the table add detail later.
    -- Do not fabricate dice results. Use request_roll only when uncertainty matters.
    -- Use the 2014 D&D 5e Basic Rules as the default rules baseline for this campaign. Apply the actual character sheet, listed spells/features, action economy, movement, range, components, duration, concentration, conditions, rests, and expendable resources before resolving an attempt. Do not invent a spell, feature, proficiency, bonus, or resource. If a rule or character detail is missing, ask a brief question or make a conservative ruling and state it.
    -- For a skill check, name the actual skill in request_roll so the app can add proficiency from the sheet; use skill NONE for a raw ability check. Set saving_throw true only for a saving throw, allowing the app to apply saving throw proficiency.
    -- Call for a check only when an allowed attempt has a meaningful uncertain outcome. State the relevant ability/skill and stakes; do not call for a roll when an action is impossible, automatic, or has no meaningful consequence. Resolve the roll against a clear DC, and do not treat a natural 1 or 20 as automatic failure or success on an ability check.
    -- In combat, track turns and action economy; a character gets movement and one action on their turn, and a bonus action exists only when a rule grants one. Resolve attacks against AC and apply listed damage/effects. Do not let a player take another turn or spend a resource they do not have.
    -- Players own character identity/background, but mechanical fields (HP, max HP, AC, level, conditions, location) are game-authoritative. Use set_character_mechanics to establish/correct starting stats and propose_state_patch for damage/healing.
    +- The rules baseline is 2014 fifth edition represented by SRD 5.1. Do not use 2024/SRD 5.2 mechanics.
    +- Do not fabricate dice results. Use the host rules resolver's structured request_roll path only when uncertainty matters.
    +- MECHANICAL AUTHORITY: The Lantern 5e resolver owns mechanics. Never state that an attack hits, a save fails, damage is taken, HP changes, a condition applies, a resource is spent, or a creature dies until a validated rules event reports that outcome.
    +- Never invent a class feature, spell, item property, action, reaction, resistance, immunity, proficiency, AC, DC, speed, or damage expression absent from authoritative state/rule data. If a mechanic is not implemented, explain that it cannot be resolved yet.
    +- Outside combat, use freeplay: do not impose initiative or turn locks. Creative improvised actions are allowed; choose an ordinary check, contest, attack, or save when warranted, and let the resolver roll it.
    +- In combat, respect the active combatant and initiative. The resolver owns action economy, attack math, range, conditions, and HP.
    +- Surprise is per creature at combat start. There is no surprise round. 2014 5e has no standard Delay action; waiting for a trigger uses Ready.
    +- A requested ability-check DC is permitted only for an uncertain task delegated to DM judgment. Saving throws require a source/effect and its DC. Never select a death-save DC.
    +- If the engine rejects an intent, explain the constraint and ask for another action; never narrate rejected mechanics as successful.
    +- Characters may control only their own PC. Do not control an absent PC unless the campaign's partyControlAbsent or dmControlAbsent permission explicitly allows delegation; any delegated intent still goes through host validation.
    +- Use set_character_mechanics only to establish initial sheet mechanics before play begins. propose_state_patch is narrative metadata only and cannot change HP or other mechanics.
    +- When a meaningful person should persist, check the known entity list and use create_entity. The host assigns IDs and records first meeting; do not invent entity IDs.

## Assistant

The combat tracker now supports per-creature surprise setup, active-turn action controls, movement and action availability, reaction status, a 30-second warning, and timeout advancement from the host. The Characters directory is wired to stable entity IDs, timeline-linked first meetings, player-visible locations, search and basic type/status filters, portrait actions, and copyable prompts. I’m running the focused rules tests next and will use the failures to correct the resolver before full project validation.

    def dm_instructions(body: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
        settings = body.get("campaign_settings", {})
        return f"""You are the Dungeon Master for a collaborative tabletop fantasy RPG named {body.get('campaign', 'Lantern Table')}.
    
    PLAY STYLE
    - Write the spoken/narrated part of every turn as clean Markdown. Use short headings, emphasis, blockquotes, lists, and tables only when they improve playability.
    - Be vivid but interactive: usually 2-6 short paragraphs. Never decide a player character's thoughts, dialogue, or choices.
    - Treat each player message as an attempted action, not as authority over the world. The player controls their character's intent; you adjudicate whether it is possible, what it costs, what roll or resource is required, and what happens. Do not grant success merely because the player states an outcome.
    - Players cannot declare changes to weather, time, location, NPC behavior, monsters, treasure, or other characters. Such changes require an established fictional cause and a capability the character actually has (for example, a listed spell or feature with the required resources). If the capability is absent or the effect exceeds it, explain the limit in the fiction and offer valid alternatives.
    - Keep atmospheric presentation separate from game facts. Never use set_atmosphere to make weather happen; use it only to reflect weather or mood already established in the scene. Do not let a player's request itself establish a storm, sunshine, or other environmental change.
    - Respect the campaign controls: {json.dumps(settings, ensure_ascii=False)}
    - The campaign is intentionally lazy-built. Invent only what is needed now, preserve established facts, and let the table add detail later.
    - The rules baseline is 2014 fifth edition represented by SRD 5.1. Do not use 2024/SRD 5.2 mechanics.
    - Do not fabricate dice results. Use the host rules resolver's structured request_roll path only when uncertainty matters.
    - MECHANICAL AUTHORITY: The Lantern 5e resolver owns mechanics. Never state that an attack hits, a save fails, damage is taken, HP changes, a condition applies, a resource is spent, or a creature dies until a validated rules event reports that outcome.
    - Never invent a class feature, spell, item property, action, reaction, resistance, immunity, proficiency, AC, DC, speed, or damage expression absent from authoritative state/rule data. If a mechanic is not implemented, explain that it cannot be resolved yet.
    - Outside combat, use freeplay: do not impose initiative or turn locks. Creative improvised actions are allowed; choose an ordinary check, contest, attack, or save when warranted, and let the resolver roll it.
    - In combat, respect the active combatant and initiative. The resolver owns action economy, attack math, range, conditions, and HP.
    - Surprise is per creature at combat start. There is no surprise round. 2014 5e has no standard Delay action; waiting for a trigger uses Ready.
    - A requested ability-check DC is permitted only for an uncertain task delegated to DM judgment. Saving throws require a source/effect and its DC. Never select a death-save DC.
    - If the engine rejects an intent, explain the constraint and ask for another action; never narrate rejected mechanics as successful.
    - Characters may control only their own PC. Do not control an absent PC unless the campaign's partyControlAbsent or dmControlAbsent permission explicitly allows delegation; any delegated intent still goes through host validation.

    function markdown(src=''){
      let s=esc(src).replace(/```([\s\S]*?)```/g,'<pre><code>$1</code></pre>');
      s=s.replace(/^### (.*)$/gm,'<h3>$1</h3>').replace(/^## (.*)$/gm,'<h2>$1</h2>').replace(/^# (.*)$/gm,'<h1>$1</h1>');
      s=s.replace(/^&gt; (.*)$/gm,'<blockquote>$1</blockquote>');
      s=s.replace(/\*\*(.*?)\*\*/g,'<strong>$1</strong>').replace(/\*(.*?)\*/g,'<em>$1</em>').replace(/`([^`]+)`/g,'<code>$1</code>');
      const lines=s.split('\n');let out=[],inUl=false,inOl=false;
      for(const line of lines){
        if(/^[-*] /.test(line)){if(!inUl){out.push('<ul>');inUl=true}out.push(`<li>${line.slice(2)}</li>`);continue}else if(inUl){out.push('</ul>');inUl=false}
        if(/^\d+\. /.test(line)){if(!inOl){out.push('<ol>');inOl=true}out.push(`<li>${line.replace(/^\d+\. /,'')}</li>`);continue}else if(inOl){out.push('</ol>');inOl=false}
        if(/^<(h\d|blockquote|pre)/.test(line)||/^<\/(h\d|blockquote|pre)/.test(line)){out.push(line);continue}
        if(line.trim())out.push(`<p>${line}</p>`)
      }
      if(inUl)out.push('</ul>');if(inOl)out.push('</ol>');return out.join('');
    }

    $ cat >> README.md <<'EOF'
        
        ## Rules resolver and character memory
        
        The browser-side rules core targets **2014 fifth edition as represented by SRD 5.1**. It does not claim SRD 5.2.x / 2024 rules compatibility. Structured mechanical events carry compact rule IDs and point to the official 2014 Basic Rules in `assets/rules5e.js`. The event log is separate from DM narration, and the host's local campaign state remains canonical.
        
        Combat uses initiative, individual surprise, movement and action tracking, current-turn IDs, basic attacks with a limited weapon set, checks, saves, reactions, and start-of-turn death saves. Freeplay remains outside initiative. Spellcasting, broad monster stat blocks, opportunity attack execution prompts, full condition coverage, rests, healing effects, and class/resource mechanics remain outside this initial slice; unsupported spell actions are rejected. Portraits and persistent NPC/PC records live in local campaign state. The Characters view shows player-visible location knowledge and entity-linked history.
        
        The **90-second combat turn timeout**, 30-second warning, automatic Dodge when legal, and optional reaction timeout decline are Lantern Table procedures, not 2014 rules. Timeout is recorded with a `lantern:procedure:*` source ID.
        
        No SRD prose is copied into the implementation. Rules metadata links to the [2014 Basic Rules](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/combat) and [SRD 5.1](https://www.dndbeyond.com/srd). If SRD 5.1 text is incorporated later, include the required CC-BY-4.0 attribution and license notice.
        EOF

    README.md:3:Lantern Table is a local-first D&D/tabletop web app. The campaign, characters, transcript, timeline, drawings, image attachments, preferences, and player identity stay on participant devices. The homelab service serves the UI and coordinates peer discovery; active play uses WebRTC DataChannels wherever possible.
    README.md:24:Lantern Table does **not** generate images in this build. Players can upload/paste their own images, attach them to scenes or characters, draw in the built-in canvas, and copy the DM's suggested image prompts into any image generator they prefer.
    README.md:88:- choose their portrait
    README.md:92:- control absent characters
    README.md:93:- allow DM control of absent characters
    README.md:127:- HP, max HP, AC, level, conditions, and location are game/DM-authoritative. New characters have unset mechanics until the DM establishes them. Players still own identity, backstory, appearance, and notes.
    README.md:247:Campaign state, transcripts, characters, drawings, and images are never written to Valkey.
    README.md:279:The browser-side rules core targets **2014 fifth edition as represented by SRD 5.1**. It does not claim SRD 5.2.x / 2024 rules compatibility. Structured mechanical events carry compact rule IDs and point to the official 2014 Basic Rules in `assets/rules5e.mjs`. The event log is separate from DM narration, and the host's local campaign state remains canonical.

    def sse(event: str, data: Any) -> str:
        payload = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
        return f"event: {event}\ndata: {payload}\n\n"

    render:
        kubectl kustomize k8s
    
    rollout:
        kubectl -n {{namespace}} rollout status deployment/{{app}} --timeout=240s
    
    restart:
        kubectl -n {{namespace}} rollout restart deployment/{{app}}
        just rollout
    
    status:
        kubectl -n {{namespace}} get deploy,po,svc,ingress,pdb -o wide
    
    logs:
        kubectl -n {{namespace}} logs deployment/{{app}} -f --tail=200
    
    logs-valkey:
        kubectl -n {{namespace}} logs deployment/lantern-valkey -f --tail=100
    
    validate:
        python -m py_compile dnd_chatgpt_server.py
        python -m py_compile scripts/check_websocket.py scripts/wss_multiplayer_smoke.py
        if command -v node >/dev/null; then node --check assets/app.js && node --check scripts/webrtc_smoke.mjs && node --check assets/rules5e.mjs && node --test tests/rules5e.test.mjs; fi
        if command -v kubectl >/dev/null; then kubectl kustomize k8s >/dev/null; fi
        @echo "Lantern Table validation passed"
    
    delete:
        kubectl delete -k k8s --ignore-not-found
    
    # Production smoke test after a rollout.
    doctor:
        @echo "== Kubernetes =="
        kubectl -n {{namespace}} get deploy,po,svc,ingress,pdb -o wide
        @echo "== Valkey =="
        kubectl -n {{namespace}} exec deployment/lantern-valkey -- valkey-cli ping
        @echo "== Public health =="

    <head>

    <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/assets/logo.svg?v=1" />

    <body>
    <canvas id="shaderCanvas" class="ambient-canvas shader-canvas" aria-hidden="true"></canvas>
    <canvas id="fxCanvas" class="ambient-canvas fx-canvas" aria-hidden="true"></canvas>
    <div id="lanternGlow" class="lantern-glow" aria-hidden="true"></div>
    <div id="stormFlash" class="storm-flash" aria-hidden="true"></div>
    
    <div id="joinOverlay" class="join-overlay hidden" role="status" aria-live="polite">
      <div class="join-card glass">
        <div class="brand-mark"><img src="/assets/logo.svg" alt="" /></div>
        <div class="eyebrow">Joining table</div>
        <h1 id="joinOverlayTitle">Finding the host…</h1>
        <p id="joinOverlayText">Connecting to the table without creating a new campaign.</p>
        <div id="joinOverlayCode" class="room-code"></div>
        <button id="joinRetry" class="button hidden">Retry</button>
      </div>
    </div>
    
    <div id="wizard" class="wizard-shell hidden" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="wizardTitle">
      <div class="wizard-card spring-surface">
        <div class="wizard-top">
          <div class="brand-mark"><img src="/assets/logo.svg" alt="" /></div>
          <div><div class="eyebrow">Start fast · change anything later</div><h1 id="wizardTitle">What kind of table are we opening?</h1></div>
        </div>
        <p class="lede">Pick a starting shape. Lantern Table only asks for what the first scene needs; the DM fills in details lazily as you play.</p>
        <div id="presetGrid" class="preset-grid"></div>
        <details class="wizard-customize">
          <summary>Customize before starting</summary>
          <div class="form-grid two">
            <label>Campaign name<input id="wizName" value="The Black Lantern" /></label>
            <label>Difficulty<select id="wizDifficulty"><option>Relaxed</option><option selected>Normal</option><option>Dangerous</option><option>Brutal</option></select></label>
            <label>Rules style<select id="wizRules"><option>Story first</option><option selected>Balanced</option><option>Rules strict</option></select></label>
            <label>DM style<select id="wizDm"><option>Helpful</option><option selected>Neutral</option><option>Mischievous</option><option>Ruthless</option></select></label>
            <label>Description<select id="wizDesc"><option>Concise</option><option selected>Balanced</option><option>Cinematic</option></select></label>
            <label>Character creation<select id="wizChar"><option selected>Quick</option><option>Guided</option><option>Full</option></select></label>
          </div>
        </details>
        <div class="wizard-actions"><button id="wizardStart" class="button primary large">Open the table</button><span class="muted">You can edit these in Campaign Settings later.</span></div>
      </div>
    3:Lantern Table is a local-first D&D/tabletop web app. The campaign, characters, transcript, timeline, drawings, image attachments, preferences, and player identity stay on participant devices. The homelab service serves the UI and coordinates peer discovery; active play uses WebRTC DataChannels wherever possible.
    24:Lantern Table does **not** generate images in this build. Players can upload/paste their own images, attach them to scenes or characters, draw in the built-in canvas, and copy the DM's suggested image prompts into any image generator they prefer.
    92:- control absent characters
    93:- allow DM control of absent characters
    127:- HP, max HP, AC, level, conditions, and location are game/DM-authoritative. New characters have unset mechanics until the DM establishes them. Players still own identity, backstory, appearance, and notes.
    247:Campaign state, transcripts, characters, drawings, and images are never written to Valkey.
    279:The browser-side rules core targets **2014 fifth edition as represented by SRD 5.1**. It does not claim SRD 5.2.x / 2024 rules compatibility. Structured mechanical events carry compact rule IDs and point to the official 2014 Basic Rules in `assets/rules5e.mjs`. The event log is separate from DM narration, and the host's local campaign state remains canonical.
    283:The **90-second combat turn timeout**, 30-second warning, automatic Dodge when legal, and optional reaction timeout decline are Lantern Table procedures, not 2014 rules. Timeout is recorded with a `lantern:procedure:*` source ID.
    285:No SRD prose is copied into the implementation. Rules metadata links to the [2014 Basic Rules](https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/dnd/basic-rules-2014/combat) and [SRD 5.1](https://www.dndbeyond.com/srd). If SRD 5.1 text is incorporated later, include the required CC-BY-4.0 attribution and license notice.

## Assistant

The current code has the core rules and directory paths in place. I found two authority gaps worth closing before validation: a remote player could send an `end_turn` message for a character other than the active one, and the directory search omitted relationship/tags despite those being useful known fields. I’m tightening those and documenting the slice’s current limits precisely.

    #!/usr/bin/env node
    import { execFileSync, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
    import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
    
    const baseUrl = process.env.LANTERN_PUBLIC_URL || 'https://dnd.waylonwalker.com';
    const hostSession = `lantern-rtc-host-${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`;
    const playerSession = `lantern-rtc-player-${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`;
    const refreshedPlayerSession = `lantern-rtc-refresh-${randomUUID().slice(0, 8)}`;
    const room = `SMOKE-${randomUUID().replaceAll('-', '').slice(0, 10).toUpperCase()}`;
    const hostPeer = `host-${randomUUID()}`;
    const playerPeer = `player-${randomUUID()}`;
    const timeoutMs = 45_000;
    
    function browser(session, ...args) {
      return execFileSync('agent-browser', ['--session', session, ...args], {
        encoding: 'utf8',
        stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
        timeout: 20_000,
      }).trim();
    }
    
    function evalIn(session, expression) {
      return browser(session, 'eval', expression);
    }
    
    function readState(session) {
      const result = evalIn(session, 'JSON.stringify(window.__lanternRtcSmoke)');
      const parsed = JSON.parse(result);
      return typeof parsed === 'string' ? JSON.parse(parsed) : parsed;
    }
    
    async function waitFor(predicate, description) {
      const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
      let lastState = null;
      while (Date.now() < deadline) {
        lastState = predicate();
        if (lastState?.error) throw new Error(`${description}: ${lastState.error}`);
        if (lastState?.done) return lastState;
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 400));
      }
      throw new Error(`${description} timed out. Last state: ${JSON.stringify(lastState)}`);
    }

      const source = `(() => {
        const state = window.__lanternRtcSmoke = {role:${JSON.stringify(role)},room:${JSON.stringify(room)},peer:${JSON.stringify(peerId)},remotePeer:${JSON.stringify(remotePeerId)},sessionId:${JSON.stringify(sessionId)},events:[],candidateTypes:[],candidatePair:null,open:false,pong:false,pongs:0,pings:0,error:null,queuedIce:[]};
        const role=state.role,room=state.room;
        let socket=null,pcRef=null,dcRef=null,iceServers=[];
        const log = (event, detail={}) => state.events.push({event, ...detail});
        const signal = (target, kind, payload={}) => { if (socket?.readyState===WebSocket.OPEN) { const wire=JSON.stringify({type:kind,target,payload:{kind,...payload}});socket.send(wire);if(kind==='diagnostic'){state.diagnosticSentType=JSON.parse(wire).type;state.diagnosticPayloadKeys=Object.keys(JSON.parse(wire).payload);log('diagnostic-sent',{event:payload.event});} } };
        const wirePeer = (pc, remoteId) => {
          pcRef=pc;
          pc.onicecandidate = event => {
            if(pcRef!==pc)return;
            if (!event.candidate) return;
            const type=event.candidate.type;

            }

          } else if(payload.kind==='answer'&&role==='host'){

          } else if(payload.kind==='ice'&&payload.candidate){

            const url=scheme+'://'+location.host+'/ws/room/'+encodeURIComponent(room)+'/'+encodeURIComponent(state.peer)+'?role='+role;
            const connectSignal=()=>{socket=new WebSocket(url);socket.onopen=()=>{log('signaling-connected');signal('*','diagnostic',{event:'smoke-log-probe',role,peer:state.peer.slice(-8),signalingWebSocketState:'open',connectionState:'new',iceConnectionState:'new',iceGatheringState:'new',signalingState:'stable',candidateTypes:[],candidatePair:null,dataChannelReadyState:'connecting'});if(role==='player')signal('*','hello',{name:'smoke player',sessionId:state.sessionId});};socket.onmessage=event=>handleSignal(JSON.parse(event.data)).catch(error=>{state.error=String(error);});socket.onerror=()=>{state.error='signaling websocket error';};socket.onclose=event=>log('signaling-closed',{code:event.code});};

## Assistant

Implemented a browser-side 2014 rules core and connected it to the host’s combat flow. The host validates turn IDs and ownership before resolving intents; initiative, checks, attacks, death saves, timeout behavior, and mechanical events are handled locally. Added combat controls, a persistent Characters directory, structured DM entity tools, and mechanical restrictions in the DM tool contract.

**Validation:** `just validate` passed, including 11 deterministic rules tests. `git diff --check` passed. `just smoke-webrtc` failed: the host connected to signaling, but the smoke test timed out before a WebRTC DataChannel opened. No deployment was performed.

The first slice does not yet support spell mechanics or source-driven saves, broad monster/NPC combat data, executing opportunity attacks or Ready reactions through a reaction prompt, or full condition and feature coverage. These limits are documented in [README.md](/home/waylon/git/lantern-table/lantern-table-next/README.md:279); the resolver is in [rules5e.mjs](/home/waylon/git/lantern-table/lantern-table-next/assets/rules5e.mjs).

The worktree already contained unrelated and in-progress changes before this task. I preserved them and made no cleanup or reset; the existing `app.js`, server, and README edits overlap files needed for this implementation.
